html:
The Chitonahua and Murunahua are small Panoan-speaking peoples of the upper Yurúa River in the Amazon rainforest of Ucayali, Peru, near the border with Brazil. Some of them still live in voluntary isolation.

They hunt, fish and farm small gardens. Their language is close to that of the Yaminahua and the Sharanahua. In the 1990s illegal mahogany loggers forced contact with some Murunahua, and disease killed many of them. Peru has since set aside the Murunahua Territorial Reserve to protect those who stay apart, near the land of the Mashco Piro.
